resources.title: 3-Tier Campus Architecture Explained
resources.description: Core, distribution, and access layers — plus when to use a collapsed core.
resources.body:
3-TIER CAMPUS MODEL

ACCESS
- End devices: PCs, phones, APs, printers
- Port security, PoE, VLAN assignment

DISTRIBUTION
- Policy, routing between VLANs, aggregation
- ACLs, summarization (as design allows)

CORE
- High-speed backbone, keep it simple and fast
- Connect distribution blocks

COLLAPSED CORE (2-TIER)
- Merge core + distribution for smaller networks
- Cheaper, fewer devices, still valid design

ASCII SKETCH
        [CORE]
       /  |  \
   [DIST][DIST][DIST]
     |     |     |
   access access access

Talk about failure domains: one access switch down shouldn't take the whole campus.

resources.title: Network Topology Types (Star, Mesh, Hybrid)
resources.description: Visual overview of common topologies with when to use each — interview and Network+ ready.
resources.body:
NETWORK TOPOLOGY TYPES (quick guide)

1) STAR
   Devices connect to a central switch.
   + Easy to manage  - Switch is critical

        PC -- Switch -- PC
                 |
                PC

2) EXTENDED STAR
   Multiple access switches under a core/distribution switch.
   Used in real buildings and campuses.

3) MESH (full or partial)
   Multiple paths between nodes for resilience.
   + Redundancy  - Cost/complexity

4) HYBRID
   What enterprises actually run: star access + hierarchical core + edge firewall.

5) BUS / RING
   Mostly exam history for modern Ethernet LANs.
   Know definitions; design with star + hierarchy.

INTERVIEW ONE-LINER
"Access layers are usually star; the campus is hierarchical; the WAN may use partial mesh."

VLANS ON A DIAGRAM

ACCESS PORT = one VLAN to a PC/phone
TRUNK = multiple VLANs between switches (802.1Q tags)

Sketch:
[PC VLAN10]--access--[SW1]==trunk==[SW2]--access--[PC VLAN20]

resources.title: Bash Backup Script Template
resources.description: Portable backup script with rotation, logging, and dry-run mode.
resources.body:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Simple backup with dry-run and rotation
set -euo pipefail
SRC="${1:-$HOME/Documents}"
DEST="${2:-$HOME/backups}"
DRY_RUN="${DRY_RUN:-0}"
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
TARGET="$DEST/backup-$STAMP"

mkdir -p "$DEST"
if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "1" ]]; then
  echo "[dry-run] Would copy $SRC -> $TARGET"
  exit 0
fi

mkdir -p "$TARGET"
cp -a "$SRC" "$TARGET/"
echo "Backup complete: $TARGET"

# Keep last 7 backups
ls -1dt "$DEST"/backup-* 2>/dev/null | tail -n +8 | xargs -r rm -rf

resources.title: Computer System Components Overview
resources.description: CPU, RAM, storage, motherboard, PSU, GPU — the big picture.
resources.body:
COMPUTER SYSTEM — BIG PICTURE

1) CPU (brain) — executes instructions
2) RAM (short-term memory) — active programs/data
3) Storage (long-term) — HDD/SSD/NVMe keep data when powered off
4) Motherboard — connects everything (buses, chipset)
5) PSU — converts wall power to usable DC rails
6) GPU — graphics/display (integrated or discrete)
7) Cooling — air/liquid keep temps safe
8) Firmware (BIOS/UEFI) — starts hardware before the OS

Data path (simple):
Input → CPU/RAM work → Storage save → Output (display/network)

BOOT CHAIN (simplified)
1) Power + PSU good
2) Firmware (UEFI/BIOS) initializes hardware

resources.title: Defense in Depth (Security Layers)
resources.description: Multiple controls so one failure isn't game over.
resources.body:
SECURITY LAYERS (DEFENSE IN DEPTH)

1) Physical — locks, badges, cable locks
2) Perimeter — firewalls, edge filtering, email security
3) Network — VLANs, ACLs, NAC, VPN
4) Host — patching, EDR/AV, hardening, host firewall
5) Application — secure config, input validation, updates
6) Data — encryption, backups, DLP, least privilege
7) Identity — MFA, strong auth, joiner/mover/leaver
8) People — training, phishing drills, process

If one layer fails, others still slow or stop the attack.

PEN TESTING ETHICS (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

✅ Written authorization (scope, dates, systems, contacts)
✅ Stay in scope — no "curious" side quests
✅ Protect client data you find
✅ Report responsibly; no public dumps

resources.body:
PATH: SECURITY LAYERS

1) CIA triad + defense in depth diagram
2) Identity layer (MFA, least privilege)
3) Endpoint layer (patch, EDR, disk crypto)
4) Network layer (segmentation, firewalls)
5) App + data layers (OWASP, encryption, backups)
6) Detection (logging) + people/process

Practice: map one real incident story to layers.
Filter the library: Security (tag: layers)

resources.body:
PATH: ETHICAL PEN TESTING

0) Ethics & law — never skip
1) Networking + Linux comfort
2) Pen test phases & reporting
3) OWASP Top 10 + WSTG intro
4) Lab platforms: TryHackMe / HTB / DVWA in YOUR VMs
5) Tool categories with permission always
6) Optional certs: PenTest+, then advanced paths

Use library category: Pen Testing
Use tools: VM Lab Wizard + Network Toolkit

resources.title: Path: Document Like a Pro
resources.description: Build a habit of logging symptoms, root cause, and fixes for tickets and interviews.
resources.body:
PATH: DOCUMENT LIKE A PRO

After every lab or ticket:
1) Open Field Journal (Tools → Field journal)
2) Use Troubleshooting or Lab template
3) Write root cause in ONE sentence
4) Tag with tech (dns, vlan, windows…)
5) Weekly: export Markdown for portfolio/backup

Interview gold: "Here's a recent issue I documented end-to-end."
